extracted.intended_audience: news organizations, newsroom editors, publishers, and journalists seeking to adopt standardized trust practices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for news organizations on adopting and displaying The Trust Project's eight standardized Trust Indicators to demonstrate newsroom trustworthiness and earn a Trust Mark. Covers required transparency, sourcing, labeling, methods disclosure, diversity, local reporting, audience feedback, and the adoption process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency about ownership, funding, and editorial policies (mission statements, ethics codes, corrections policies, masthead).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish clear information on who owns and funds the outlet and the newsroom's editorial policies; provide mission statements, ethics codes, a visible masthead, and an accessible corrections policy so audiences can evaluate institutional transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist Expertise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reporter bylines with biographical information and qualifications (e.g., beats, education, relevant experience) so readers can assess the reporter's expertise and authority on the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of Work / Labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear labels distinguishing news, opinion, analysis, sponsored content, advertorial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly label content formats (news vs. opinion vs. analysis vs. sponsored/advertorial) to prevent audience confusion about purpose and standards applied to the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations & References
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources, documents, data linked or cited within stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to or cite primary sources, documents, datasets, and supporting materials within stories so readers can verify claims and follow the evidence behind reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the story reported? Why this story? Disclose process for investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain reporting methods (interviews, FOIA requests, data analysis, on-the-ground reporting), decision rationale, and investigation process to make journalistic practices transparent and reproducible where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally Sourced
rubrics_metrics.description: Was reporter present in the location? Reliance on local voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether reporting involved on-the-ground presence and use of local sources or voices; emphasize local sourcing when location-specific knowledge or context matters for credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse Voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsroom efforts to include diverse perspectives across social, ideological, demographic differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document newsroom practices and story sourcing that aim to include a range of perspectives (social, ideological, demographic) to reduce bias and improve representativeness in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms for audience to engage, challenge, suggest, correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear channels for audience engagement (comments, corrections submission, contact methods) and show how feedback is handled so readers can challenge or contribute to reporting and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption Process for Trust Mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary; eligibility review; cohort training and implementation; Trust Mark awarded after compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations choose to participate; they undergo eligibility review, receive cohort training, implement the Trust Indicators, and are awarded a Trust Mark after meeting compliance requirements—this process is procedural and serves as a compliance/quality pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency as quality (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An implicit standard that transparency (about ownership, funding, policies, methods) functions as a core measure of journalistic quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that visible institutional and methodological transparency improves audience trust and should be embedded across practices (links to Best Practices, Methods, Citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological rigor (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An implicit expectation that reporting demonstrates methodological rigor in sourcing, fact-checking, and investigative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely tied to Methods and Citations & References: audiences evaluate trustworthiness by how rigorously information was gathered and verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local presence as credibility (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An implicit belief that reporter presence or strong local sourcing increases credibility for location-specific stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals such as on-the-ground reporting and local voices count as evidence of credibility and help distinguish coverage quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity as quality (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An implicit standard that inclusion of diverse perspectives constitutes a marker of better journalistic quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity in sourcing and newsroom practices mitigates bias and broadens the accuracy and fairness of coverage (related to Diverse Voices indicator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience accountability (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An implicit requirement that newsrooms be accountable to audiences through feedback and correction mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms that allow audience challenge and correction are treated as essential to maintaining trust and are operationalized via Actionable Feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing rigor (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An implicit emphasis on rigorous sourcing practices—verifiable, credited, and diverse sources—as a trust metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages linking to primary documents, naming sources when appropriate, and documenting verification steps (overlaps with Citations & References).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction of genres (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An implicit standard that correctly distinguishing content genres (news vs. opinion, sponsored vs. editorial) affects trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear genre labeling reduces confusion about intent and standards applied to a piece; practical implementation appears in the Type of Work / Labels indicator.
